q: How can an automotive supplier in Morocco get renewable electricity that counts in market based Scope 2?
title: Morocco: renewable power for suppliers
short: Three common routes: a private supply contract from a wind or solar producer under Morocco's renewable energy law, rooftop or on site solar under the self generation rules, or certificates where available. Each counts only with a contract, metered delivery and proof the attributes are not claimed twice.
audience: Car part, harness and textile suppliers in Tangier, Kenitra and Casablanca asked by European buyers to raise renewable share

ul: Private supply: renewable producers can sell to customers connected at medium, high or very high voltage.
Self generation: on site solar, with rules on grid connection and surplus.
Certificates: check that they meet Scope 2 quality criteria for your market.
Attribute retirement or a clause that the producer will not sell them elsewhere.

p: Eligibility, voltage levels and grid fees change with new regulations, so check the current rules before signing.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills and solar generation records into a dated, fingerprinted record, so the kWh behind a market based claim trace back to the documents.
